Check Conditions

Source: R/utils_checks.R
entrata_abort_check.Rd

These functions are specialized versions of the entratar condition functions that are intended for use in the package's internal checking functions. They create conditions with specific classes that can be used to identify and handle errors, warnings, and messages.

Usage

entrata_abort_check(
  msg,
  ...,
  parent = NULL,
  call = rlang::caller_env(),
  .envir = parent.frame()
)

entrata_warn_check(
  msg,
  ...,
  call = rlang::caller_env(),
  .envir = parent.frame()
)

entrata_inform_check(
  msg,
  ...,
  call = rlang::caller_env(),
  .envir = parent.frame()
)

check_abort(
  msg,
  ...,
  parent = NULL,
  call = rlang::caller_env(),
  .envir = parent.frame()
)

check_warn(msg, ..., call = rlang::caller_env(), .envir = parent.frame())

check_inform(msg, ..., call = rlang::caller_env(), .envir = parent.frame())

Arguments

msg

Character string or vector containing the message to be displayed. This gets passed to cli::cli_bullets() allowing for cli's custom formatting, glue interpolation, inline markup syntax, and other features.

...

Passed to rlang::abort(), rlang::warn() or rlang::inform().

call

The execution environment of a currently running function, e.g. call = caller_env(). The corresponding function call is retrieved and mentioned in error messages as the source of the error.

You only need to supply call when throwing a condition from a helper function which wouldn't be relevant to mention in the message.

Can also be NULL or a defused function call to respectively not display any call or hard-code a code to display.

For more information about error calls, see Including function calls in error messages.

.envir

Environment to evaluate the glue expressions in.

Value

These functions do not return values, but are used for their side effects, namely creating and signaling conditions. The entrata_abort() function will stop execution, while entrata_warn() & entrata_inform() will allow execution to proceed.

Details

The condition class hierarchy is structured like so:

where <entrata_condition> is the base class for all entratar conditions and sits on top of the existing rlang and base R condition classes.

For example, an entrata error thrown without any additional custom class added to it using entrata_abort() will have the following classes:

[1] "entrata_error" "entrata_condition" "rlang_error" "error" "condition"

This allows for filtering and handling of Entrata-specific conditions while still being compatible with the broader R condition system.

Functions

  • entrata_abort_check(): creates an entrata_error condition for checks.

  • entrata_warn_check(): creates an entrata_warning condition for checks.

  • entrata_inform_check(): creates an entrata_message condition for checks.

Aliases

  • check_abort(): alias for entrata_abort_check()

  • check_warn(): alias for entrata_warn_check()

  • check_inform(): alias for entrata_inform_check()

See also

Utility Functions: entrata_active_config

Conditions: entratar-conditions

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
entrata_abort("This is a entratar error.")

# catch a condition and check its classes
err <- rlang::catch_cnd(entrata_abort("Error Message"))
class(err)

# catch a warning and check its classes
wrn <- rlang::catch_cnd(entrata_warn("Warning Message"))
class(wrn)

# catch a message and check its classes
msg <- rlang::catch_cnd(entrata_inform("Message"))
class(msg)
} # }
